title: Live termal.sqlite WAL stays at 1.4 GB across a clean restart: no truncating checkpoint or journal_size_limit
outcome: Observed 2026-09-04 on the live store: termal.sqlite 2.08 GB with termal.sqlite-wal 1.43 GB before a clean stop, and the WAL file still 1,427,666,552 bytes after the server was stopped, rebuilt and restarted (15:12 local). SQLite reuses a WAL from offset 0 after a checkpoint but never shrinks the file unless PRAGMA journal_size_limit is set or a TRUNCATE checkpoint runs; a 1.4 GB WAL also means long stretches without a completed checkpoint while the server was running (external readers are already forbidden, so the likely holders are long-lived internal read transactions or the write cadence). Investigate: (1) whether the persist path or the boot path ever runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) or sets journal_size_limit; (2) which connections hold read transactions long enough to block checkpoints; (3) an idle-time or shutdown TRUNCATE checkpoint and a journal_size_limit (e.g. 64 MB) so the WAL returns to a bounded size. Acceptance: after a clean shutdown the WAL is bounded (<= journal_size_limit); during normal operation the WAL does not grow past the limit for more than one checkpoint interval; no change to the fail-closed startup validation; measured on a backup copy, never on the live file.
